sources.title: Trending Rust repositories on GitHub this month

output.findings:
The Rust ecosystem is currently dominated by high-momentum developer tooling and AI agent infrastructure. Leading the pack is 'farion1231/cc-switch' (31,143 stars this month), a cross-platform assistant for managing various coding agents like Claude Code and Gemini CLI. 'Hmbown/CodeWhale' (35,709 stars this month) follows as a terminal-based DeepSeek coding agent, while 'openai/codex' (8,651 stars this month) remains a key lightweight terminal agent.

Other notable dev-tooling projects include '1jehuang/jcode' (4,681 stars this month), a coding agent harness, and 'ogulcancelik/herdr' (3,228 stars this month), an agent multiplexer for the terminal. 'xingkongliang/skills-manager' (859 stars this month) provides a specialized utility for syncing AI agent skills across multiple coding environments, and 'ryoppippi/ccusage' (1,751 stars this month) offers essential cost-tracking for agentic CLI workflows.

Why they matter:
- farion1231/cc-switch: Simplifies the fragmented landscape of AI coding agents into a single interface.
- Hmbown/CodeWhale: Represents the shift toward terminal-native, high-performance AI coding agents.
- openai/codex: Provides a foundational, lightweight agentic experience for terminal users.
- 1jehuang/jcode: Standardizes the harness for developing and testing coding agents.
- ogulcancelik/herdr: Enables efficient management of multiple AI agents simultaneously.
- xingkongliang/skills-manager: Bridges the gap between different AI coding tools by centralizing skill management.
- ryoppippi/ccusage: Critical for developers monitoring the economic impact of agentic workflows.

2. Hmbown/CodeWhale (35,709 stars): A high-performance terminal-based coding agent leveraging DeepSeek.
3. xingkongliang/skills-manager (859 stars): A desktop utility to sync and organize AI agent skills across various coding environments.
4. ryoppippi/ccusage (1,751 stars): Essential tooling for monitoring token consumption and costs of local agentic CLI tools.
5. ogulcancelik/herdr (3,228 stars): A terminal-based agent multiplexer for managing multiple AI agent sessions efficiently.

output.findings:
The trending landscape is dominated by agentic tooling and AI-driven development workflows. In Python, high-momentum projects include 'academic-research-skills' (Claude Code research workflows, 21,719 stars this month), 'CloakBrowser' (stealth automation, 21,656 stars), 'ai-engineering-from-scratch' (educational, 20,541 stars), 'MoneyPrinterTurbo' (AI video generation, 20,221 stars), 'markitdown' (Microsoft's file-to-markdown tool, 18,736 stars), and 'headroom' (token-efficient RAG/MCP proxy, 3,209 stars).

In Rust, the momentum is heavily focused on high-performance agentic infrastructure and developer tooling. Top projects include 'cc-switch' (multi-agent CLI manager, 31,143 stars this month), 'CodeWhale' (DeepSeek-powered terminal agent, 35,709 stars), 'RuView' (spatial intelligence, 19,186 stars), 'openai/codex' (terminal coding agent, 8,651 stars), 'liteparse' (fast document parser, 3,934 stars), and 'herdr' (agent multiplexer, 3,228 stars).

These repositories highlight a clear shift toward local-first, high-performance agentic tooling. Python remains the primary language for high-level agent orchestration and research-focused workflows, while Rust is increasingly the choice for performance-critical agent infrastructure, terminal-based multiplexers, and low-latency document processing.
